body:
- `validatePresense` probably shouldn't be added for any field unless explicitly asked for. 
- For `created` and `modified` fields I don't think any validation rules need to be added by default. 
- Use of both `allowEmpty` and `notEmpty` isn't very newbie friendly, makes things look confusing.
Can you take care of those points @ADmad ?
I can give it a shot but would have to wait for couple of weeks at least :)  Going on a break from next week and have other things to take care of this weekend.

body: If we didn't use `allowEmpty()` and `notEmpty()` what should take their place? `validatePrescence()` is used for non-nullable fields.

> If we didn't use allowEmpty() and notEmpty() what should take their place?

I didn't mean don't use either of them. I meant if possible don't use both.

> validatePrescence() is used for non-nullable fields.

Non-nullable doesn't necessarily mean you want to save it each time. I have seen numerous times on IRC newbies tripping after over zealously adding `'required' => true` for fields.

Thanks for picking this op so quickly.

I agree with @ADmad, cake is known for it's newbie friendliness, that's why I started with it myself some years back and not with Zend & stuff.

If crud & validations work right away after baking without too much config & considerations, it will give any newbie the confidence to continue the journey.

`ValidationSet::$_allowEmpty` is false by default so wouldn't calling `Validator::notEmpty()` for each field with just field name be redundant? It would only make sense calling it if non default values for args `$message` and `$mode` are passed too, which isn't the case in baked code.
Doh I realized that `validatePresense` is only used on `create`. In that case it seems reasonable. Just removing it for `created` and `modified` should be enough.
@NoobsAllowed That is why I started using CakePHP as well. Obviously 3.0 is a work in progress and there are still some work to be done, but feedback like this is great for finding rough patches.
